title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 66
paragraphs: Thus far, then, had this battle gone. Artabazos son of Pharnakes, however, had been displeased from the very first that Mardonius remained behind after the king had gone, and afterwards had continually raised objections and done nothing, always urging them not to fight a battle. Since he was not pleased with what Mardonius was doing, for himself he acted as follows. The men under his command — and he had with him no small force, as much as forty thousand — when the fighting began, knowing well what the outcome of the battle would be, he led them carefully, having first given orders that all should go by the way he led them and at the same pace he went. Having given these orders, he led his troops on the pretense of taking them into battle; and when he was well on his way, he saw the Persians already in flight. Then he no longer led his men in the same order as before, but set off at a run, fleeing by the quickest route — not to the palisade or to the wall of the Thebans, but toward Phokis, eager to reach the Hellespont as quickly as possible.
